answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable deposit before trading, with the deposit growing each time a new identity is created from the same hardware or funding source. A fake identity is like an island with no ivory trade route and no basalt foundation: it looks impressive from afar but carries no real weight, since its deposit stays frozen until honest peers attest its completed work. Forging a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand deposits, more than the attack can earn back.
